evidence: Traupman 161: exercēre ūnum ex artificiīs, to practise one of the trades
terms.comment: The occupation of a craftsman (Lewis & Short); Traupman’s word for a trade.

terms.gloss: a skill; the craft or profession one lives by
evidence: Ov. Met. 3.588: ars illī sua cēnsus erat
M-O s.v. work, job: career, profession
terms.comment: In Cicero both the crafts and the learned professions (Off. 1.150–151).

terms.gloss: a living, a way of making money
evidence: M-O s.v. work, job: quō quaestū tē tenēs?, what do you do for a living?
terms.comment: For the trade as a living rather than a skill; Cicero pairs it with artificium (Off. 1.150).

phrases.english: his trade was all his wealth

phrases.latin: litterae thēsaurum est, et artificium nunquam moritur
phrases.english: learning is a treasure, and a trade never dies (a freedman speaking)
